title: Java ArrayList
learningObjectives: Add, access, update and remove elements.
Use size and contains to inspect a list.
Traverse a list with a loop.
Choose ArrayList when indexed access is important.

understand.concept: ArrayList is a resizable implementation of the List interface. It stores elements in insertion order, supports duplicates and provides fast indexed access in typical use. Its size grows as elements are added. Use a generic type such as ArrayList<String> to make the element type explicit. ArrayList stores object references, so primitive values use wrapper types such as Integer. Removing an element shifts later indexed elements.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java arraylist in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: Import java.util.ArrayList and declare the element type with angle brackets. add appends an element; get reads an index; set replaces an element; remove deletes by index or matching object. size reports the current number of elements. Enhanced for loops are convenient for reading every element. Removing while iterating with an ordinary for-each loop can cause ConcurrentModificationException; use an Iterator or removeIf for safe conditional removal.

examples.title: Create and append
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<String> names = new ArrayList<>(); names.add("Mira"); names.add("Ravi"); System.out.println(names); } }
examples.explanation: add appends elements and ArrayList grows automatically.

examples.title: Access by index
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<String> cities = new ArrayList<>(); cities.add("Delhi"); cities.add("Pune"); System.out.println(cities.get(1)); } }
examples.explanation: List indexes start at zero, so get(1) returns the second element in the list.

examples.title: Update an element
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<Integer> scores = new ArrayList<>(); scores.add(7); scores.add(9); scores.set(0, 8); System.out.println(scores); } }
examples.explanation: set replaces the value at an existing index.

examples.title: Remove an element
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<String> tasks = new ArrayList<>(); tasks.add("Read"); tasks.add("Write"); tasks.remove(0); System.out.println(tasks); } }
examples.explanation: remove by index deletes that position and shifts following elements.

examples.title: Loop and total
examples.code:
import java.util.ArrayList;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayList<Integer> values = new ArrayList<>(); values.add(2); values.add(4); values.add(6); int total = 0; for (int value : values) total += value; System.out.println(total); System.out.println(values.size()); } }
examples.explanation: An enhanced for loop visits each value while size reports the element count.

questions.explanation: ArrayList implements List and can grow or shrink.

questions.prompt: Which method reads an element by index?
questions.explanation: get(index) returns the element at that position.
set updates the value at an existing index.

questions.prompt: Which type is used for an ArrayList of integers?
questions.explanation: Generics require reference types; Integer wraps int.

questions.prompt: What happens after removing an element by index?
questions.answer: Later elements shift to lower indexes
options: Later elements shift to lower indexes
questions.explanation: ArrayList closes the gap by shifting later elements.
